notes: elixir-ecto/ecto: elixir-ast (tier B): 576 alias, import, require and use statements naming a literal module in 126 files (0 the parser rejected); 435 edges to the file(s) whose defmodule defines the module (nested defmodules expanded; a self-reference is no edge), 117 statements name a module no subject file defines (Logger, a dependency), 18 name no static module (`alias __MODULE__.Foo`, `use unquote(m)`), counted and never listed

file_edge_precision and file_edge_recall measured against an import dump's (file, imported file) pairs, there being no SCIP index: the truth is what each file's import statements name, not the files its references reach as a SCIP index's cross-file edges are, so a file reached without an import of its own (a file another one required, an autoloaded constant) is outside the truth and a resolved edge to it counts against precision, while a file imported and never referenced is in it (LB-F57)

import_resolution: 740 of 751 in-repo imports resolve to a file the oracle names (11 unresolved, 0 only to other files; L3 bar: excellent >= 0.95, good >= 0.85); import edges precision 0.9971 (699 of 701) and recall 1 (699 of 699); 2 of 1095 imports resolved where the oracle names no file of the subject; 0 oracle imports on no statement fathom extracted; 0 oracle import targets outside the files measured
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)

phoenixframework/phoenix: elixir-ast (tier B): 524 alias, import, require and use statements naming a literal module in 177 files (0 the parser rejected); 305 edges to the file(s) whose defmodule defines the module (nested defmodules expanded; a self-reference is no edge), 199 statements name a module no subject file defines (Logger, a dependency), 9 name no static module (`alias __MODULE__.Foo`, `use unquote(m)`), counted and never listed

Subjects: phoenixframework/phoenix v1.8.9 (734c8d1c, 177 .ex/.exs files) and elixir-ecto/ecto v3.14.2 (f6eb4929, 126), whole repositories, tests and integration suites included. Oracles: L1 elixir-ast (Elixir 1.19.6's own parser, calibration/oracles/elixir-ast, tier B), L2 the grammar's own tags.scm run by py-tree-sitter (tier C, independent runtime, not independent query shape: the dialect's tags.scm started from it), L3 elixir-ast's alias/import/require/use statements resolved to the file whose defmodule defines the module (tier B). Tier B and C cap every level at good.

universal-ctags 6.2.1, the row's named oracle, is not the L1 grade (design D2, observation O1327): it tags `def`/`defmodule` inside heredocs (119 def, 50 defmodule, 22 defp oracle-only on Phoenix) and ends modules at them. Against ctags the same dialect reads sym_recall .9302 and .9617, sym_precision .9985 and .9997, kind_agreement 1, signature_coverage 1 and range_agreement .5965 and .5857 on Phoenix and Ecto, which is level none at L1 on range alone. ExUnit `test` blocks (2,877 in the two subjects) are extracted (kind ElixirTest, canonical `test`) and outside the scored kinds: ctags writes their names with spaces, which the harness's last-segment name rule cannot compare.

L3: import_resolution .9854 (740 of 751 in-repo statements; module-to-file by namespace-dir over the dialect's captured package, so a module defined in a file its name does not spell, several to a file, resolves) with file_edge_precision 1 and file_edge_recall .401. The recall is the cost of O1328: a statement draws no edge of its own (module_symbol cannot combine with a captured package), only a call the import binds does; the dotted-module + snake_case alternative reads import_resolution .62/.72 on lib/ and is not the dialect's strategy. `alias Foo.Bar` binds the full name (O1329), so `Bar.fun()` after it binds nothing; `Foo.Bar.fun()`, `as: B` and group members bind.

Calls: call_recall .976 and call_precision .9664 against the grammar's own query (tier C). A call in a definition's own head and a built-in type written in a `@spec` are also calls (O1329); module-level macro calls are the module's (the module kind is callable) and a test's calls are its module's. Not extracted: defexception, defstruct, operator definitions, unquote'd names. Elixir 1.19.6 (compiled for OTP 27) ran on OTP 29.1.2 for the oracle; fathom never runs Elixir.
